extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers and conference authors (NeurIPS community)
extracted.subtask_description: A report describing the NeurIPS 2019 reproducibility program components (code submission policy, community reproducibility challenge, and a reproducibility checklist), how they were deployed, and lessons learned for improving reproducibility in machine learning research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility: obtaining similar results as presented in a paper or talk, using the same code and data (when available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducibility is a necessary step to verify the reliability of research findings; it promotes open and accessible research, allowing the community to integrate findings and convert ideas to practice. It also encourages robust experimental workflows which can reduce unintentional errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A code submission policy (one of the three components of the NeurIPS 2019 reproducibility program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring or encouraging submission of code alongside papers to enable others to reproduce results. Presented as a program component intended to improve community standards for how ML research is conducted, communicated, and evaluated. (The page notes the policy was deployed as part of the NeurIPS 2019 program; specific submission requirements are described in the full report/PDF rather than the abstract.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-wide reproducibility challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: A community-wide reproducibility challenge (one of the three components of the NeurIPS 2019 reproducibility program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An organized challenge to have community members attempt to reproduce published results, thereby generating independent verification and insights about reproducibility practices. The abstract frames this as a mechanism to learn about and improve reproducibility across the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine Learning Reproducibility checklist (submission requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of the Machine Learning Reproducibility checklist as part of the paper submission process (one of the three components of the program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding a reproducibility checklist into submissions to raise standards and prompt authors to provide information needed for reproducibility (e.g., code/data availability, experimental details). The abstract states this was included in the submission process to improve standards; the checklist's specific items are in the full document rather than the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness and reliability of presented/published results
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented and published results should be sound and reliable (an overarching desideratum motivating the program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring soundness/reliability is tied to reproducibility efforts; reproducibility checks and policies are framed as necessary steps to verify claims and reduce unintentional errors through more robust experimental workflows.
